data.why: The app bundles all example data internally: example_data.py embeds a full receptor+ligand PDB (imatinib/Abl, PDB 1IEP) for Docking Validation, guides.sample_files()/omics_io.demo_dataset() generate downloadable demo expression, group, survival (Freireich 1963) and docking-enrichment CSVs in-app, and reference_compounds.py supplies a GBM drug SMILES library for Compound Screening -- so every core workflow has a one-click 'Try example data' / 'Built-in example' path needing no external upload.

goals: Screen a candidate SMILES for Lipinski/Veber/BBB drug-likeness and blood-brain-barrier penetration before committing to docking
Validate a docking setup by redocking a known crystallographic ligand (imatinib/Abl, built-in example) and confirming RMSD <= 2.0 A
Dock a researcher-supplied ligand SMILES into an uploaded or fetched receptor structure and inspect binding energy, pose ranking and contacts
Fit a 4-parameter logistic dose-response curve to concentration/response pairs and read off an IC50 estimate
Run Kaplan-Meier survival curves and a log-rank test on a two-group time/event dataset, or compute ROC AUC / enrichment factor for docking actives vs decoys
Run differential expression (Welch/Mann-Whitney + BH-FDR) and PCA/volcano visualization on a gene x sample expression table against group labels

review.summary: The tree describes the reachable parts of OncoAgent-GBM accurately, with well-pitched general labels and screens that support the claims (one weak citation). It still needs fixes before filing: blocked tasks should be marked as such, t16 belongs in the triage phase, the literature, enrichment and docking-setup parts of the app are missing, and two lift-able docking components should be added as features.
